phases.name: Foundation
phases.progression_rule: Reps first, then sets, then tempo, then a harder variation: work each exercise to the top of its rep range for all sets, then add one set (max 4), then slow the eccentric to 3 seconds, then move to the next variation (e.g. incline push-up -> full push-up, dead hang -> negatives -> band-assisted pull-up). Runs: complete the C25K intervals for the week; never chase pace, only completion.
phases.boundary_note: Weeks 1-2 are deliberately sub-maximal to build the 5:30 AM habit. If a session is missed, do not double up the next day. By end of week 5 targets: 3x10 full push-ups, 3x5 negative pull-ups (5s down), 30s plank x3, C25K week 5 completed (first 20-min continuous run).

phases.name: Progression
phases.progression_rule: Double progression with load: for weighted lifts work from 3x8 to 3x12, then increase dumbbell weight ~2.5kg and drop back to 3x8. Pull-ups: negatives -> band-assisted -> first strict rep -> add singles until 3x5. Oblique/core work 3x/week (Mon/Wed/Sat blocks). Runs: extend continuous running each week (C25K weeks 6-9), then consolidate 25-30 min continuous so a full 5K is run by ~week 12.
phases.boundary_note: WEEK 6 EQUIPMENT DECISION (the 2x2.5kg dumbbells and 4kg kettlebell are now too light for lower-body and row strength work): either buy adjustable dumbbells or join a gym. Option A budget: plate-loaded 20kg adjustable set (Kore 20kg combo ~Rs.700-1,200 promo pricing on Amazon.in, Bullar 20kg cast-iron ~Rs.2,500-3,500 estimated). Option A premium: Boldfit Powerflex dial-adjustable 2.5-24kg pair, Rs.16,999 on boldfit.com (listed ~Rs.14,999 on Amazon.in). Option B: gym membership in Indiranagar - Cult SELECT/ELITE from ~Rs.1,155-1,470/month on long-commitment passes; independent gyms Rs.1,000-6,500/month (Gold's Gym Rs.4,800/mo, Snap Fitness Rs.4,700/mo, Figurine Rs.3,000/mo, budget gyms ~Rs.1,000-2,000/mo). The plan's weighted exercises (floor press, rows, RDLs, lunges, carries) assume ~20-24kg total is available from week 6.

phases.name: Cut & Define
phases.progression_rule: Keep lifting loads (do NOT drop weights while cutting - strength work preserves muscle in a deficit); progress by density instead: shave 15s off circuit rest each week, add one circuit round every 2 weeks, cap RPE 8. Two metabolic circuits/week (Wed full session + Sat finisher: KB swing + burpee + push-up + mountain climber). Three runs/week (Tue intervals, Fri easy, Sat long). Core 4x/week (Mon/Tue/Thu/Sat). Week 21 is a DELOAD: halve all sets, drop the Sat finisher, all runs easy 20-30 min.
phases.boundary_note: WEEK 14 SHIFT: training volume stays similar but intent changes from building to defining - a modest calorie deficit does the cutting, training preserves muscle and raises weekly energy burn. Strength moves consolidate into two full-body days to make room for the second metcon and third run. If sleep or 5:30 AM energy degrades, cut the deficit before cutting the training.

exercises.reps: C25K session of the week (wk1: 60s run/90s walk x8)
repeat the week's C25K session (Cubbon Park loop)
C25K wk6-9 session; from wk10: 6-8 x 2min brisk / 1min easy
work up to 3x5 strict (band-assist as needed)
wk6-9: longest C25K continuous block; wk10-13: 25-40 min easy - run full 5K by wk12
8-10 x 1min hard / 90s easy, or 5 x 3min @ 5K effort
15 (finisher with burpee x8 + push-up x10 + mountain climber 30s)

exercises.name: Push-up (wall -> incline -> knee -> full progression)
exercises.cue: Body one straight line - squeeze glutes so the hips never sag or pike.

exercises.name: Incline push-up (hands on table/wall)
exercises.cue: Same rigid plank as a full push-up - only the angle changes, not the form.

exercises.name: Decline push-up (feet on chair) - PRIMARY dip substitute
exercises.cue: Hands slightly ahead of shoulders; don't let the head dive - lead with the chest.

video.note: Same progression video - decline is the 'harder variation' step of the push-up ladder

exercises.name: Chair dips (bench dips, feet on floor) - ALTERNATIVE dip substitute
exercises.cue: Hips brush the chair edge and elbows point straight back; stop at upper-arm-parallel - deeper strains the shoulder.

exercises.name: Standing resistance band chest press
exercises.cue: Brace like a plank - press with the chest, don't twist or lean into the band.

exercises.name: Pike push-up
exercises.cue: Head travels forward-and-down toward a spot ahead of your hands, not straight down.

exercises.name: Dumbbell floor press (no-bench bench press)
exercises.cue: Upper arms at ~45 degrees from the torso; touch triceps to floor softly, never bounce.

exercises.name: Standing dumbbell shoulder press
exercises.cue: Squeeze glutes and ribs down - if the lower back arches, the weight is too heavy.

exercises.name: Dead hang
exercises.cue: Shoulders active - pull shoulder blades slightly down instead of hanging on the joint capsule.

exercises.name: Negative (eccentric) pull-up
exercises.cue: Jump to chin-over-bar, then fight gravity for a full 3-5 seconds - never just drop.

exercises.name: Band-assisted pull-up
exercises.cue: Drive elbows down to your ribs - think 'pull the bar to your chest', not 'chin over'.

exercises.name: Pull-up (strict)
exercises.cue: Start every rep from a dead stop with active shoulders - no kipping.

exercises.name: Inverted row under a sturdy table (or band row)
exercises.cue: Squeeze shoulder blades together before the arms bend; body stays a rigid plank.

exercises.name: One-arm dumbbell row
exercises.cue: Pull the elbow to your hip, not your armpit - no torso twist to heave the weight.

exercises.name: Goblet squat
exercises.cue: Elbows track inside the knees at the bottom - chest tall, heels glued down.

exercises.name: Bodyweight squat (deep)
exercises.cue: Sit between your heels, not behind them - full depth with heels down beats half reps.

exercises.name: Split squat
exercises.cue: Drop the back knee straight down under your hip - the front shin stays near vertical.

exercises.name: Dumbbell reverse lunge
exercises.cue: Step back, then push the floor away through the FRONT heel to stand.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Romanian deadlift
exercises.cue: Push the hips straight back with soft knees until the hamstrings scream - the spine never rounds.

exercises.name: Kettlebell swing (two-hand)
exercises.cue: It's a hip HINGE and snap, not a squat or a front raise - the arms are just ropes.

exercises.name: Glute bridge
exercises.cue: Posterior-tilt first (tuck the tailbone), then squeeze up - lift with glutes, not lower back.

exercises.name: Standing calf raise
exercises.cue: 3-second lowering into a full stretch at the bottom - the stretch is where calves grow.

exercises.name: Farmer's carry / suitcase carry
exercises.cue: Walk tall as if balancing a book on your head - no leaning toward the weight.

exercises.name: Plank (forearm)
exercises.cue: Squeeze glutes and abs so hard the body trembles slightly - a saggy 60s is worse than a hard 30s.

exercises.name: Side plank
exercises.cue: Stack shoulder over elbow and push the hips UP and slightly forward - no sagging.

exercises.name: Dead bug
exercises.cue: Lower back stays welded to the floor - if it arches, shorten the leg reach.

exercises.name: Bird dog
exercises.cue: Reach LONG (heel back, fingers forward) keeping hips level - a glass of water on your back shouldn't spill.

exercises.name: Hollow body hold
exercises.cue: Press the lower back into the floor first, then extend limbs only as far as that contact holds.

exercises.name: Hanging knee raise
exercises.cue: Curl the pelvis up at the top (tuck tailbone toward navel) - lifting knees alone is just hip flexors.

exercises.name: Russian twist
exercises.cue: Rotate the ribcage, not just the arms - shoulders turn, eyes follow the hands.

exercises.name: Bicycle crunch
exercises.cue: Slow and controlled - shoulder toward opposite hip, don't yank the neck.

exercises.name: Mountain climber
exercises.cue: Hips stay level with the shoulders - speed is worthless once the plank breaks.

exercises.name: Burpee
exercises.cue: Snap the hips back under you before you jump - land soft with knees tracking over toes.

exercises.name: Run/walk intervals (C25K style)
exercises.cue: The run segments should be slow enough to speak full sentences - most beginners run them twice too fast.

exercises.name: Easy run (conversational)
exercises.cue: Nose-breathing-possible pace; short quick steps (~170+ per minute) beat long lopes.

exercises.name: Long run
exercises.cue: Slowest run of the week on purpose - finish feeling like you could do 10 more minutes.

exercises.name: Active recovery brisk walk
exercises.cue: Brisk but easy - this is a recovery tool, arriving sweaty means it was too hard.

exercises.name: Dynamic warm-up (5-8 min follow-along)
exercises.cue: Move through ranges you'll train today - raise heart rate and joint temperature, don't fatigue.

exercises.name: World's greatest stretch
exercises.cue: Long spine in the lunge; rotate the chest open toward the front leg and reach tall.

exercises.name: Cat-cow
exercises.cue: Move one vertebra at a time with the breath - exhale round, inhale extend.

exercises.name: Ankle mobility (knee-to-wall rocks + calf stretch)
exercises.cue: Drive the knee over the toes with the heel nailed to the floor.

exercises.name: 90/90 hip stretch
exercises.cue: Both knees at 90 degrees; hinge the chest over the front shin with a straight back.

exercises.name: Band shoulder dislocates (pass-throughs)
exercises.cue: Wide grip, straight arms, slow arc - narrow the grip only over weeks.

exercises.name: Cool-down stretch + breathing (5 min follow-along)
exercises.cue: Hold each stretch ~20-30s and lengthen the exhale - end with 5 slow nasal breaths.

dip_substitute.alternative: Chair dips (feet on floor, shallow range)
dip_substitute.why: For a previously sedentary desk worker, bench/chair dips load the shoulder in deep extension + internal rotation - exactly the position tight anterior shoulders tolerate worst, and the most common dip-related impingement complaint. The decline push-up uses the same chair, trains the same pressing muscles (chest/triceps/front delts) with MORE load than a flat push-up, keeps the shoulder in a safe pressing plane, and slots directly into the Hybrid Calisthenics push-up progression already in the program (progress: flat 3x10 -> decline). Chair dips stay as the alternative for triceps-focused variety once shoulder mobility improves - with strict rules: hips brushing the chair, elbows pointing back, stop at upper-arm-parallel. Pseudo-planche push-ups were rejected: they are a skill-level movement (wrist and straight-arm scapular strength) inappropriate for weeks 1-5 of a beginner program.

channels.name: Hybrid Calisthenics
channels.why: Hampton's wall-to-full progressions for push-ups/pull-ups/squats are the exact ladders this program uses - the friendliest beginner coaching on YouTube.

channels.name: Calisthenicmovement
channels.why: Crisp 2-5 minute technique breakdowns (plank, push-up, rows) with common-mistake corrections.

channels.name: Squat University
channels.why: Dr. Aaron Horschig (DPT) on ankle/hip mobility and pain-free squatting - the go-to when something starts aching.

channels.name: Mark Wildman
channels.why: The most systematic kettlebell teaching series on YouTube - his numbered swing/clean progressions fit a single-4kg-KB household perfectly.

channels.name: Renaissance Periodization
channels.why: Dr. Mike Israetel's exercise-technique series covers every dumbbell lift in Phase 2-3, plus evidence-based fat-loss guidance for the Phase 3 cut.

channels.name: Jeff Nippard
channels.why: Research-referenced technique and program-design videos - ideal once adjustable dumbbells or a gym arrive at week 6.

channels.name: FitnessBlender
channels.why: No-hype follow-along videos - the 5-minute warm-up and cool-down slots in every session can just play these.

channels.name: The Running Channel
channels.why: Beginner-friendly running form, pacing and couch-to-5K content for the Tue/Sat run slots.

c25k.pattern: 5 min warm-up walk, then 60s run / 90s walk x 8
5 min walk, then 90s run / 2 min walk x 6
5 min walk, then 2 x (90s run, 90s walk, 3 min run, 3 min walk)
5 min walk, then 3 min run, 90s walk, 5 min run, 2.5 min walk, 3 min run, 90s walk, 5 min run
3 sessions build: 5/3/5/3/5 -> 8 run/5 walk/8 run -> 20 min continuous run

c25k.mapping_note: Program has 2 dedicated run days (Tue + Sat), not 3: do the week's key C25K session Tuesday and repeat/consolidate it Saturday (Sat adds the KB-swing finisher in Phase 1). Program week N = C25K week N through week 9; weeks 10-12 consolidate 25-30 min continuous so a full 5K is run by ~week 12, matching the Phase 2 goal. Resource (verified): NHS Couch to 5K - https://www.nhs.uk/live-well/exercise/running-and-aerobic-exercises/get-running-with-couch-to-5k/ ; explainer video (verified): https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_1b-0Vlmfa4 (Marathon Handbook).
